title: U.S. House · Ohio's 9th District
area: Northwest Ohio along Lake Erie, including Toledo and Lucas County.

context.text: Ohio's congressional map was redrawn for 2026, changing the 9th District's boundaries from those used in 2024. Analysts said the new lines favor Republicans more than the old ones did: Kaptur won by 13 points in 2022 under the old lines, while Trump carried the new district's territory by about eleven points in 2024 (an estimated 54.8%-44.2% Trump-Harris under the 2026 lines, per The Downballot). Incumbent Marcy Kaptur (D) ran unopposed in the May 5 Democratic primary. Derek Merrin (R), a former Ohio House member, won a five-way Republican primary with 44.1% of the vote. Libertarian Matthew Althaus won his primary but was later disqualified from the November ballot. Kathy McKinstry filed as an independent write-in candidate.

summary.text: Marcy Kaptur is the Democratic incumbent seeking re-election in Ohio's 9th Congressional District, which she has represented since 1983. A Toledo native and former urban planner who worked in the Carter administration, she is the longest-serving woman in the history of Congress and sits on the House Appropriations Committee. Her campaign website describes her as a fighter for jobs and Great Lakes protection who represents the "Big Middle."

background.text: Born in Toledo, Ohio, in 1946. According to her official biography, she is Polish-American, grew up in a family that ran a small grocery store, still lives in the Toledo house where she grew up, and was the first member of her family to attend college after graduating from St. Ursula Academy.
Earned a bachelor's degree in history from the University of Wisconsin (1968) and a master's in urban planning from the University of Michigan (1974).
Worked as an urban planner with the Toledo-Lucas County Plan Commissions (1969-1975) and as director of planning at the National Center for Urban Ethnic Affairs (1975-1977).
Served as an urban policy advisor in the Carter administration (1977-1979); her official biography says she helped move 17 housing and neighborhood revitalization bills through Congress in that role.

Was pursuing a doctorate at MIT when Lucas County Democrats recruited her to run for Congress in 1982. She defeated first-term Republican incumbent Ed Weber and took office on January 3, 1983, becoming the first woman to represent Ohio's 9th District.

Serves on the House Appropriations Committee, including its subcommittees on Defense, Energy and Water Development (ranking member) and Agriculture, Rural Development, Food and Drug Administration, and also serves on the House Budget Committee. She previously served on the Banking, Veterans' Affairs, Agriculture and Oversight committees.

Became the longest-serving woman in the history of Congress. Her official biography credits her with securing federal funding for northwest Ohio projects including the I-280 Veterans' Glass City Skyway, Toledo's Farmers' Market and the Ottawa National Wildlife Refuge visitors center.

Author of the book Women in Congress: A Twentieth Century Odyssey (Congressional Quarterly, 1996); received an honorary Doctor of Laws from the University of Toledo (1993) and the 2002 Ellis Island Medal of Honor, according to her official biography.

priorities.text: Jobs, costs and the economy: says strengthening the economy is her top priority, and that she is fighting to bring jobs back to Ohio, remove tax breaks from companies that ship jobs overseas, and secure tariffs to protect Ohio-based manufacturers.
Supports job training and technical-skills programs as an alternative path to good-paying work that doesn't require a four-year degree.
Says she has fought to protect Social Security and Medicare from cuts and privatization.

positions.summary: Her campaign website says she is fighting for tariffs to protect Ohio-based factories and companies from unfair trade agreements.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Appropriations (119th Congress, 2025-2026), including the Agriculture-Rural Development-FDA, Energy and Water Development, and Defense subcommittees.
Was ranking member of the Appropriations Subcommittee on Energy and Water Development in the 118th Congress (2023-2024) and chaired that subcommittee in the 117th Congress (2021-2022).

summary.text: Derek Merrin is the Republican nominee for Ohio's 9th Congressional District. He began in local office in Waterville, Ohio, served as an Ohio House member from Lucas County from 2016 to 2024, including as chair of the Health and Ways and Means committees, and was the 2024 Republican nominee for this seat. According to his campaign website, he is running on lower taxes, simplifying the tax code and transparency.

background.text: Born in Smithtown, New York; moved with his family to Waterville, Ohio, at age 13 and graduated from Monclova Christian Academy in 2005.

Earned a B.A. from the University of Toledo (2008), a master's in public administration from Bowling Green State University (2009) and a public performance measurement certificate from Rutgers University-Newark.
Worked as a business owner, realtor and state auditor, including for Ohio Auditor Dave Yost; his campaign website describes him as a real estate investor.
Joined Waterville City Council at age 19 and was elected mayor of Waterville two years later, serving as mayor from 2008 to 2011, according to his campaign website.

Entered the Ohio House in 2016, appointed to finish the term of Rep. Barbara Sears after she resigned, and won election to the seat that November. He was re-elected in 2018, 2020 and 2022, representing District 47 and, after redistricting, District 42; he did not run again in 2024 and left office on December 31, 2024.

Chaired the Ohio House Health Committee (2019-2020) and the Ways and Means Committee (2021-2022); his campaign website also describes him as an elected leader of the House Republican Caucus. In 2022 he lost the vote for Speaker of the House to Jason Stephens, 54 to 43.

According to his campaign website, bills he sponsored or advanced include the Epinephrine Accessibility Act (HB 101), the Down Syndrome Non-Discrimination Act (HB 214) and a repeal of the sales tax on prescription eyewear (HB 116).
Was the 2024 Republican nominee for this seat and lost to Marcy Kaptur under the previous district lines, 48.3%-47.6%. According to his campaign website, he lives in Monclova Township.

priorities.text: Says he is a strong advocate for lower taxes, simplifying the tax code, and promoting transparency, citing his role leading efforts in the Ohio legislature to cut the state income tax.
Says he advocated for policies to reduce health-care costs, promote price transparency, and expand patient access through fewer regulations as chairman of the Ohio House Health Committee.

positions.summary: His campaign website says he successfully led efforts to cut Ohio's state income tax and is a strong advocate for lower taxes.
His campaign website says he led efforts to expand school choice while in the Ohio legislature.
Voted yes on SB 215 (allowing adults 21 and older to carry a concealed handgun without a permit), which passed the Ohio House 58-36 on 2022-03-02.

stated.summary: His campaign website says he played a key role in Ohio's constitutional-carry law allowing Ohioans to carry firearms without a permit.

record.text: Voted yes on SB 215 (allowing adults 21 and older to carry a concealed handgun without a permit), which passed the Ohio House 58-36 on 2022-03-02.

As an Ohio House member, sponsored and passed HB 116 repealing the state sales tax on prescription eyewear, and HB 592 repealing the Financial Institution Tax on Small Business Investment Companies, according to his campaign.

Sponsored the Epinephrine Accessibility Act (HB 101) and the Down Syndrome Non-Discrimination Act (HB 214), and a bill simplifying the process for homeowners to challenge their property valuations (HB 118), according to his campaign.
Chaired the Ohio House Ways and Means Committee in the 134th General Assembly and previously chaired the House Health Committee.
